title: Relative pseudo-coherence can be tested on every affine polynomial chart
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a locally finite type morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], [def-pc-morphism-conventions], let $E\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category], and let $m\in\mathbf Z$. Then $E$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent relative to $S$ [def-sfb-relative-pseudo-coherent-complex] if and only if, for every pair of affine open subschemes $U\subset X$ and $V\subset S$ with $f(U)\subset V$, every integer $n\geq0$, and every closed immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^n_V$ over $V$, the object $Rj_*(E|_U)$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent on $\mathbf A^n_V$ [def-pc-derived-direct-image]. Such an embedding exists for each pair $(U,V)$, with $n$ allowed to depend on the pair. Absolute $m$-pseudo-coherence here has the local strictly perfect approximation meaning specified in [def-sfb-m-pseudo-coherent-complex]; restrictions to open subschemes are derived pullbacks as in that definition. Relative affine space has the meaning of [def-nagata-relative-affine-space], and closed immersions that of [def-weil-closed-immersion].

source.place: Tag 09UJ, lemma-relative-pseudo-coherence-characterize, together with Tag 09VC, lemma-relatively-pseudo-coherent (some embedding if and only if every embedding)

proof.text: For any affine pair $(U,V)$ in the statement, [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs] makes $A=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_X)$ a finitely generated algebra over $R=\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_S)$. Choose finitely many generators $a_1,\ldots,a_n$. Evaluation gives the surjection $R[T_1,\ldots,T_n]\twoheadrightarrow A$. The affine description of relative affine space and of closed immersions identifies its spectrum with the required embedding $U\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^n_V$. This proves the existence assertion independently of $E$.

source.place: Tag 01T2, lemma-locally-finite-type-characterize, recalled immediately before Tag 09UI

proof.text: Assume $E$ is relatively $m$-pseudo-coherent. Choose the affine covers $V_a$, $U_{ab}$ and their good embeddings from [def-sfb-relative-pseudo-coherent-complex]. Fix arbitrary affine $U,V$ and $u\in U$. Pick $a,b$ with $f(u)\in V_a$ and $u\in U_{ab}$. Apply [lem-sc-affine-inter-principal-both] on $S$ to get $f(u)\in V'\subseteq V\cap V_a$, principal in both $V$ and $V_a$. Put $U_0=U\cap f^{-1}(V')$ and $X_0=U_{ab}\cap f^{-1}(V')$. Pulling back their defining sections makes these principal affine opens of $U$ and $U_{ab}$. Apply the same common-principal-neighborhood lemma on $X$ to $U_0,X_0$ at $u$, obtaining $U'_u$ principal in both. It is also principal in $U$: a principal open $D_{D(t)}(s/t^q)$ equals $D_U(ts)$ after representing its defining section in the localization. Thus these $U'_u$ cover $U$ by principal opens.

source.place: Tag 09UJ, lemma-relative-pseudo-coherence-characterize, common principal neighborhoods in its proof; Schemes Tag 01IW

proof.text: Restrict the chosen good embedding $i_{ab}:U_{ab}\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^{n_{ab}}_{V_a}$ to the open subscheme $\mathbf A^{n_{ab}}_{V'}$. The resulting embedding $i_0:X_0\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^{n_{ab}}_{V'}$ has $Ri_{0*}(E|_{X_0})\cong(Ri_{ab*}(E|_{U_{ab}}))|_{\mathbf A^{n_{ab}}_{V'}}$ by [lem-pc-restrict-derived-direct-image-open]. This is $m$-pseudo-coherent: restrict the local strictly perfect approximations in [def-sfb-m-pseudo-coherent-complex] to this open. Their cohomology isomorphisms and degree-$m$ surjections restrict as well. Relative affine space has the indicated open restriction by its affine coefficient-localization description. The morphism $X_0\to V'$ is finite type since its ring of sections is the quotient of the finite-variable polynomial ring defining $i_0$.

source.place: Tag 09UJ proof, restriction to the common principal base open; Cohomology Tag 08FE, lemma-restrict-direct-image-open

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-affine-principal-relative-pseudocoherence-localization] with its ambient affine base $S$ equal to the present $V$, its standard open equal to $V'$, its affine source equal to $X_0$, and its principal source open equal to $U'_u$. Step 3 supplies the good embedding over $V'$. The lemma gives a good embedding of $U'_u$ into finite-dimensional affine space over $V$. This is valid for every $u\in U$.

source.place: Tag 09VD, lemma-localize-relative-pseudo-coherent, applied as in Tag 09UJ

proof.text: The affine morphism $U\to V$ is finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs]. Its principal cover $(U'_u)_{u\in U}$ has the good embeddings over the fixed base $V$ supplied in step 4. Apply [lem-sfb-affine-principal-relative-pseudocoherence-gluing] to obtain one good embedding of $U$ over $V$. For every other closed embedding $j:U\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^n_V$, [lem-sfb-affine-polynomial-embedding-pseudocoherence-invariance] gives $m$-pseudo-coherence of $Rj_*(E|_U)$. Since $(U,V)$ was arbitrary, this is the forward implication.

source.place: Tag 09UJ, reduction to a principal cover by Tag 09VE; Tag 09VC for every embedding

proof.text: Conversely assume the stated condition for every affine pair and every embedding. Choose an affine cover of $S$ and affine covers of its inverse images, using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. For each pair choose an embedding as constructed in step 1. The hypothesis says its derived pushforward is $m$-pseudo-coherent. These covers and embeddings are exactly the witnesses required by [def-sfb-relative-pseudo-coherent-complex]. Hence $E$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent relative to $S$.

source.place: Tag 09UJ, implication (2) to (1), directly from Tag 09UI
